Indonesian authorities have arrested three people for allegedly tapping President Prabowo Subianto’s phone. Police say the suspected unlawful surveillance also targeted officials, politicians, journalists, NGO representatives and businesspeople. Investigators have seized electronic devices and the suspects face up to 10 years in prison if convicted.

JAKARTA (Reuters) – Indonesian police have named a fourth senior officer as a suspect in the alleged wiretapping of President Prabowo Subianto, as authorities continue to investigate the motives behind a scandal that has exposed a deepening rift between the president and his predecessor, Joko Widodo.

An Indonesian military helicopter carrying eight people on a firefighting mission crashed into waters off Borneo on Wednesday, killing one crew member. Indonesia has been battling wildfires across Sumatra, Borneo and Papua, with smoke spreading to neighbouring countries.
